resourceBoundary.policy: Complete 4096-byte correlated property-edit request/receipt or typed refusal; no writable JS document mirror or binary resource payload. Native bake admits at most 8 MiB conservative scratch before sampling; each retired expression VM retains its existing 4096-byte input, 8 MiB heap, 256 KiB stack and 32-poll ceilings. Resource refusal is typed unavailable and never partially commits.

semantics: Typed native object.property.edit intent: setValue(frame, values), setKey(frame, values), removeKey(frame), setAnimated(frame, animated), bake(), setExpression(code), setExpressionEnabled(enabled), removeExpression(). Bake evaluates the existing stored expression through the bounded native runtime across the whole native composition and preserves the original 0.005 key/curve optimization and constant-value rule. It atomically replaces keys or static value and disables that expression in ONE history entry. Callers cannot provide sampled values or keys; failed evaluation leaves the document untouched. Stable contextId/layerUid and optional strokeId identify the holder; property is an opaque native selector. Frames preserve finite negative/fractional values; vectors contain 1..4 finite components with native-owned dimension/applicability validation. The native revision/history owner alone resolves static versus keyed writes and animation transitions. Changed edits add exactly one revision/history entry; no-op adds none and preserves redo. setExpression(code) replaces the exact authored source (<=4096 UTF-8 bytes; the empty string stays present-but-empty, a new expression starts disabled and an existing enabled flag is kept), setExpressionEnabled(enabled) flips enablement and keeps the code, and removeExpression clears the expression; each is ONE revision/history entry through the same owner, never evaluates, and keeps invalid syntax as authored data for the existing evaluator diagnostic. The order and timeRemap selectors stay unavailable. No caller-authored custom curvePoints, JS evaluator, metadata-based write grant or legacy fallback is admitted. Existing D12 property-track controls remain separate. Public route admission does not establish ordinary installed UI acceptance.
